lead_headline: Dispatch logs 47 commits in a single day as audio, podcast, and admin architecture converge
lead_body: Dispatch had its busiest single day on record. Forty-seven commits resolved a run of audio routing failures, graduated the podcast subsystem from scaffolding to a coherent feature, and closed the day by migrating project management logic out of the admin panel and into individual project pages.
lead_article:
Dispatch had its busiest single day yet. Forty-seven commits landed across a full sprint that touched audio routing, SEO, the podcast subsystem, frontend polish, architecture docs, and a late-night admin refactor. The audio stack alone accounts for a dozen fixes — presigned-URL resolution moved to deterministic keys, the TTS path was wired into all synthesis routes, the crossOrigin attribute that was silently breaking playback got removed, and the backend fallback now takes precedence over R2 when audio is missing. The podcast feature graduated from scaffolding to something coherent: index and detail merged into a single page, the audio proxy was restructured twice to get nested key routing right on Vercel, and the subtitle copy was corrected. SEO and social sharing shipped alongside a social preview image, README corrections, and a round of doc alignment to match actual codebase state. The evening closed with project management logic moving out of the admin panel and into individual project pages — a structural shift that will make the admin surface considerably quieter.

Astro had a substantial day of its own. The advanced-routing flag was lifted in a dedicated PR, meaning that feature is now on by default. X-Forwarded-* header resolution merged into FetchState, closing a reported regression. Background dev mode was redesigned: the `astro dev background` subcommand was replaced with an `--background` flag, a cleaner surface that also got proper SIGTERM handling and improved lockfile error reporting. A markdown processor abstraction landed alongside a new `@astrojs/markdown-satteri` package, and the Cloudflare adapter now skips the SSR build for fully static sites. Claude Code, meanwhile, shipped v2.1.152 and absorbed a wave of incoming reports — two ralph-wiggum fixes merged addressing Stop-hook command quoting on Windows and an assistant-transcript read bug — but the volume of open issues suggests the release has friction on several platforms simultaneously.
